threads.body: For `rpc`, the fallback path currently ignores the new `stability_opt_in_list` (and even the existing `otel.semconv-stability.opt-in`) and only considers `otel.semconv-stability.preview`. This means declarative `general.stability_opt_in_list` cannot enable stable RPC semconv when no per-domain `rpc.semconv` is provided.

This test asserts that legacy declarative config (`general.semconv_stability.opt_in`) is ignored for the `db`/`database` domain. If the intended precedence is new declarative (`stability_opt_in_list` or per-domain `db.semconv`) → legacy declarative (`semconv_stability.opt_in`) → flat fallback, then this expectation should be inverted (i.e., legacy declarative should still be honored when the newer config is absent).

For `messaging`, the fallback path currently ignores `general.stability_opt_in_list` (and `otel.semconv-stability.opt-in`) and only considers `otel.semconv-stability.preview`. This prevents the newer declarative opt-in list from affecting messaging semconv selection when no per-domain `messaging.semconv` is set.

`resolveSemconvSelection(...)` currently falls back from per-domain `*.semconv` directly to `stability_opt_in_list` (if non-empty) and then to flat properties, but it never consults the legacy declarative shape `general.semconv_stability.{opt_in,preview}` (except for `service.peer`). This appears to contradict the stated precedence (new declarative → legacy declarative → flat fallback) and can break existing declarative-config users who relied on `general.semconv_stability.*`.

This test asserts that legacy declarative `general.semconv_stability.preview` is ignored for `rpc`. If legacy declarative config is still meant to be supported as an intermediate fallback (new declarative → legacy declarative → flat), then `semconv_stability.preview` should continue to influence selection when no newer per-domain `rpc.semconv` is provided.

This test asserts that legacy declarative `general.semconv_stability.preview` is ignored for `messaging`. If legacy declarative config is still expected to be supported as a fallback when the newer per-domain `messaging.semconv` config is absent, this expectation should be updated to reflect that legacy declarative preview still affects selection.

System-property fallback parsing doesn’t trim or drop empty entries. Values like "rpc, messaging" will include a leading space and won’t match the contains() checks in shouldEmitStable/shouldEmitOld, leading to unexpected behavior. Consider applying the same trim/filter logic used for stability_opt_in_list.

threads.body: `v3Preview` is documented (in the PR description) as forcing stable semconv emission for all domains except messaging, but `resolveSemconvSelection(...)` currently returns per-domain `semconv.version` selections before applying `v3Preview`. That means a config like `general.db.semconv.version=0` (or `dual_emit=true`) can override v3-preview and re-enable legacy (or dual) emission unexpectedly.

replies.body: No code change needed. `v3Preview` should only affect fallback/default selection; explicit per-domain `semconv.version` / `dual_emit` config is intended to take precedence. I updated the PR description to clarify that behavior.

threads.body:
`rpc` (and `service.peer`) fallback selection is currently driven only by `previewValues`. That means the long-standing `otel.semconv-stability.opt-in=rpc` / `...=service.peer` setting (and its `general.semconv_stability.opt_in` declarative equivalent) will no longer enable stable semconv when `general.stability_opt_in_list` is unset, which is a backwards-incompatible behavior change and conflicts with existing repo guidance/tests that use `-Dotel.semconv-stability.opt-in=rpc`.

Consider including the legacy opt-in set alongside preview when computing the fallback values for `rpc` and `service.peer` (so both legacy flags keep working) while still honoring the new `stability_opt_in_list` and per-domain `semconv.*` precedence.

threads.body:
`resolveStableOptInValues()` currently unions `general.stability_opt_in_list` with legacy `otel.semconv-stability.opt-in` (and `general.semconv_stability.opt_in`) values. That means the legacy opt-in can still enable domains even when `stability_opt_in_list` is explicitly set, which contradicts the PR’s stated precedence: `general.<domain>.semconv.*` > `general.stability_opt_in_list` > fallback.

To match that precedence (and to allow an explicitly empty `stability_opt_in_list` to disable opt-ins), treat the presence of `stability_opt_in_list` as authoritative and only fall back to legacy opt-in when the key is absent.
